summary: You need 135 graduate units, including at least 57 letter-graded units of coursework (the four core energy courses, the three foundational courses, and technical electives your advisor approves), at least 36 units of ENERGY 363 research, 7 units of the ENERGY 352 seminar and ENERGY 358 for teaching; the seminar, teaching and research units do not count toward the 57. Your advisor confirms that the electives are technical and that at least half of them are at the 200 level or higher, and checks the 3.25 cumulative and 2.7 quarterly GPA, transfer units, and courses shared with a PhD minor. The written exam, proposal defense, the 39 units for candidacy, the oral exam and the dissertation are recorded by the department.

children.name: Core and Foundational coursework
children.desc: The PhD program requires completion of seven mandatory courses, consisting of four core energy courses and three foundational courses. All students are expected to complete these seven core and foundational courses, regardless of whether they enter the PhD program with a BS or an MS. A student may be exempted from one or more courses upon demonstrating equivalent prior preparation through coursework or experience. Any exemption must be approved by the student’s advisor and the Graduate Standing Committee.

children.name: Foundational Courses
children.desc: Students also complete three courses in mathematics and numerical methods. These courses provide the analytical, computational, and modeling foundations necessary for graduate-level work in energy systems.

children.name: Technical Electives
children.desc:
Remaining required coursework beyond the core and foundational classes and up to the required 57 credits should be selected in consultation with, and approved by, the student’s primary PhD advisor and aligned with the student’s research topic. At least half of these courses must be at the 200 level or higher, and all must be taken for a letter grade.
Technical electives may include graduate-level courses in Energy Science and Engineering and related disciplines. Students are encouraged to develop depth in a particular area through coherent sets of courses (theme-based sequences), when appropriate.
children.notes:
The 57 units of coursework post BS degree is a minimum; in some cases, the research advisor may specify additional requirements to strengthen the student’s expertise in particular areas.
The 57 units of coursework exclude the required teaching experience (ENERGY358: Doctoral Degree Teaching Requirement) and required research seminars (ENERGY352: ESE Graduate Seminar).
